behaviors.description: When the salamander enters or exits water, it changes the form of its molecular structure to mimic its surroundings. Other than its AC, its statistics are the same in each form. Any object it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.
behaviors.descriptionWithLinks: When the salamander enters or exits water, it changes the form of its molecular structure to mimic its surroundings. Other than its AC, its statistics are the same in each form. Any object it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.
behaviors.name: Shifting Molecules

behaviors.description: The salamander can breathe air and water.
behaviors.descriptionWithLinks: The salamander can breathe air and water.
behaviors.name: Amphibious

behaviors.description: The salamander can move through other creatures and objects no more than 10 feet in diameter as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) kinetic damage if it ends its turn inside an object.
behaviors.descriptionWithLinks: The salamander can move through other creatures and objects no more than 10 feet in diameter as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) kinetic damage if it ends its turn inside an object.
behaviors.name: Diffuse Body

behaviors.description: The salamander can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.
behaviors.descriptionWithLinks: The salamander can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.
behaviors.name: Spider Climb

behaviors.description: Any creature that grapples the salamander takes 3 (1d6) kinetic damage at the end of its turn.
behaviors.descriptionWithLinks: Any creature that grapples the salamander takes 3 (1d6) kinetic damage at the end of its turn.
behaviors.name: Spiked Hide

behaviors.description: While underwater, the salamander has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide, and it can take the Hide action as a bonus action.

behaviors.name: Watery Stealth

name: Mucous Salamander
sectionText: Mucous salamanders, or pinkish salamanders, are amphibians native to the bogs of Yavin 4. They possess the distinct ability to diffuse their molecular structures underwater, which allow them to swim faster and pass through hunters' nets. When a mucous salamander enters dry areas, it cN change its molecular structure into hardened scales for protection from predators, particularly the angler.
speeds: 30 ft., climb 30 ft. (solid form), swim 50 ft. (liquid form)
